title: How to enlarge cursor in Photoshop on Mac: expert tips for better brush visibility
metaTitle: How to enlarge cursor in Photoshop on Mac: Expert Guide
description: Learn how to enlarge cursor in Photoshop on Mac by using built-in brush settings and shortcuts instead of system-wide pointer scaling that causes bugs.
intro: In Photoshop on Mac, there is no direct setting to enlarge the cursor size independently of your system settings. To improve visibility, you should adjust the brush tip preferences or use keyboard shortcuts to resize your brush dynamically.
tldr: Avoid changing system-wide mouse pointer size in macOS Accessibility settings as it causes brush alignment bugs.
Use Photoshop Preferences to change your cursor from a crosshair to a full brush tip.
Hold Control and Option while dragging your mouse to resize your brush visually on the canvas.
Use the bracket keys on your keyboard to quickly grow or shrink your brush diameter.

blocks.text: Why you should not use system-wide cursor scaling

Many Mac users attempt to enlarge their cursor by going to System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Pointer size. While this makes your arrow cursor larger across macOS, it creates a significant issue within Photoshop. The application often fails to scale the brush tool correctly when the system pointer is enlarged. This leads to a mismatch between the visual cursor and the actual area being painted. You might find that your brush paints several pixels away from where the center of your cursor appears. This makes precise work impossible. For professional graphic design, you must keep the system pointer size at the default setting.

If you struggle to see your cursor, the best approach is to change how Photoshop displays the brush tip. You can choose between a simple crosshair or a preview of the actual brush size. Open your preferences to modify these settings.

items: Open Photoshop and click on Photoshop in the top menu bar.
Select Settings or Preferences from the dropdown menu.
Choose Cursors from the sidebar list.
Under Painting Cursors, select Normal Brush Tip to see the actual size of your brush.
Check Show Crosshair in Brush Tip if you need a center point for extreme accuracy.
Click OK to save your changes.

blocks.text: The fastest way to resize brushes

Instead of changing a static cursor size, most designers use dynamic resizing. This allows you to scale your brush up or down instantly while you work. The most effective method involves a simple keyboard and mouse combination. Hold down the Control and Option keys at the same time. While holding these, click and drag your mouse to the right to increase the brush size. Dragging to the left will decrease it. You will see a red overlay on your canvas that represents the brush diameter. This provides immediate visual feedback without needing to open any menus.
Using keyboard shortcuts for brush control

Keyboard shortcuts are the backbone of a fast Photoshop workflow. You do not need to hunt for sliders in the Options bar to change your brush size. Use the bracket keys on your keyboard for quick adjustments. Pressing the left bracket key decreases your brush size by a set increment. Pressing the right bracket key increases it. If you add the Shift key to these shortcuts, you can change the brush hardness at the same time. This is useful when you need to switch between a soft, feathered edge and a hard, crisp line.
Common cursor issues and how to fix them

Sometimes your cursor might change unexpectedly. A common issue is the brush turning into a crosshair. This happens when you accidentally press the Caps Lock key. Simply press Caps Lock once to toggle your brush tip back to its normal state. If your cursor feels laggy, check your Photoshop performance settings. High-resolution files with many layers can slow down the brush preview. Ensure you have enough RAM allocated to Photoshop in the Performance section of your preferences. If you are using a very old version of Photoshop, consider updating via the Creative Cloud app to ensure compatibility with newer macOS versions.

Adobe offers both a desktop version and a web-based version of Photoshop. The desktop version provides the full range of cursor preferences and custom brush settings. The web app is designed for simplified tasks and collaboration. It lacks the deep preference menus found in the desktop version. If you require precise control over your cursor appearance or advanced brush dynamics, stick to the desktop application. The web app is better suited for quick edits or sharing files with clients who need to leave comments.

faq.question: Why is my Photoshop cursor a crosshair?
faq.answer: Your cursor has likely turned into a crosshair because the Caps Lock key is active. Press the Caps Lock key once to return the cursor to its standard brush tip appearance.

faq.question: Can I make the Photoshop cursor larger in macOS settings?
faq.answer: You can change the system pointer size in macOS settings, but it is not recommended. Doing so often causes a bug where the visual cursor does not align with the actual brush pixels, leading to inaccurate painting.

faq.question: What is the best way to resize a brush quickly?
faq.answer: The best method is to hold the Control and Option keys while dragging your mouse horizontally on the canvas. This shows a live preview of the brush size and hardness.

task: How to enlarge cursor in Photoshop on Mac

steps.name: Change cursor preferences
steps.text: Go to the Photoshop menu, select Settings, then Cursors. Choose Normal Brush Tip to ensure you see the full size of your brush.

steps.name: Use the resize shortcut
steps.text: Hold Control and Option while dragging your mouse left or right to visually resize your brush on the canvas.

steps.name: Toggle Caps Lock
steps.text: If your brush appears as a crosshair, press the Caps Lock key on your keyboard to restore the brush tip view.

troubleshooting.problem: Brush paints in the wrong spot
troubleshooting.fix: Set your macOS pointer size back to Normal in System Settings > Accessibility > Display.
Check if your Caps Lock key is turned on and disable it.
